title: Carter Caves & Cascade Falls
summary: In Carter County, more than twenty caverns honeycomb the limestone along Tygarts Creek, and Cascade Cave joined the state park there in 1959.
bodyMarkdown:
Carter Caves State Resort Park lies along Tygarts Creek in [Carter County](https://grokipedia.com/page/Carter_County,_Kentucky), Kentucky. The park protects a karst landscape of more than 20 caves, along with natural bridges carved from Mississippian-age limestone. It is one of the state's best places to see how water shapes stone underground.

## People in the hills

Long before the park, Native peoples used this country. Surveys have recorded more than 265 prehistoric and historic sites in Carter County. Most reflect Native occupation from the Paleo-Indian period through the Late Prehistoric era, with seasonal hunting and flint quarrying.

The area served as hunting land for Shawnee and Cherokee groups and was crossed by trails such as the Warrior's Path. Artifacts from the area point to short-term use rather than permanent villages.

## Saltpeter and private hands

The caves had practical uses early on. Saltpetre Cave at [Carter Caves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carter_Caves_State_Resort_Park) was mined during the War of 1812, because saltpeter (potassium nitrate) is a key part of gunpowder. Today the Saltpetre Cave tour focuses on that history, told more fully in [Saltpeter Cave at Carter Caves](/stories/saltpeter-cave-at-carter-caves/).

The land stayed in private hands for almost 200 years. In 1946 the last owners, the J.F. Lewis family, joined other investors and local Rotary Clubs in donating 945 acres to the Commonwealth of Kentucky. Gov. William Jason Fields, a Carter County native, pushed for the purchase of the caves and land.

## Cascade Cave

Cascade Caves were added to the park in 1959. Cascade Cave is really three caves in the same area and together forms the largest cave in the park. It has an underground lake room and a 30-foot underground waterfall.

Other caves offer different views. X Cave is named for its crossing passages and has some of the park's largest rock formations. Bat Cave is left unimproved and is toured as a "wild" cave in summer.

## Bridges and protected species

The park's trails pass seven natural bridges. The largest, Smokey Bridge, stands 90 feet high and 120 feet wide. The Natural Bridge Trail passes beneath another, the only natural bridge in Kentucky that is paved and carries traffic.

On December 16, 1981, 146 acres of the park became state nature preserves. They protect the endangered Indiana bat, which hibernates in Bat Cave, along with mountain maple and Canada yew. Bat Cave and Saltpetre Cave close in winter because of white-nose syndrome, a disease that threatens several bat species.

## Kentucky today

Carter Caves is a state resort park with a lodge, cottages and a campground. Visitors can take guided tours of Cascade Cave and X Cave all year and hike more than 26 miles of trails. Laurel Cave and other non-commercial caves can be explored in summer with a permit.
